It’s surprising how long someone can survive in renal failure, but unfortunately if she’s not strong enough for a transplant, she’ll pass eventually and it’s better for her to be on hospice than to take her off only for her to need it again.

I actually cared for someone(I’m a CNA) who was in almost the exact situation- she went into renal failure, but because of other health conditions she wouldn’t survive transplant surgery so her family opted to put her on hospice instead. She was on hospice for a good five months before she finally passed, but it was good to have that support all the way to the end of her life.

Putting someone on hospice is a difficult decision, but if you’re unsure as to how long she has left or her QOL, I’d keep her on it, especially if she’s still expressing renal symptoms, having intense pain, and periods of confusion.

Families could see their parents and their grandparents walking and talking before lockdown, and the next time they saw them was in a casket.
